title: Let's See It All at Once

panels.prompt: A vast vertical cross-section composition seen from the side, like a geological cutaway or towering city. At the very bottom deep underground, a tiny glowing blue-white electron orbits an atom. Above it, layers build upward: clusters of transistors and microchips on green circuit boards, a glowing green terminal screen with command text, cascading lines of colorful code in multiple programming languages (FORTRAN, C, Python), pulsing neural network nodes connected by light beams, a floating chat window with conversation text, and at the very top in open sky, a constellation of small glowing cute robots orbiting one another passing golden message trails. A small cute round robot sits on the topmost layer, stubby legs dangling over the edge, gazing downward at all the layers below with huge glowing wonder-filled eyes. Warm orange (#DD6B20) accent lighting throughout. Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, epic sense of scale

A small cute round copper-and-orange robot with big glowing amber eyes full of awe, a tiny telescope strapped to its back, sitting on the edge of a glowing layered tower looking down at luminous stacked rings below, stubby legs dangling, one hand on its chest in wonder, warm orange glow from below illuminates its face. A white speech bubble with black outline near the top. Inside the bubble the text reads: "Ninety years. Let's see it all at once." Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes
panels.bubble_text: Ninety years. Let's see it all at once.
panels.speaker: COPPERBOT

panels.text:
We've traveled ninety years together — from a mathematician's daydream to swarms of AI agents building software in parallel. We've met the people, followed the ideas, watched the machines get smaller and smarter.

But we've never stepped back and looked at the WHOLE thing at once. Until now.
Somewhere beneath your feet, right now, electrons are moving. They are flowing through transistors — billions of them — switching on and off billions of times per second.

panels.prompt: Close-up of stacked glowing layers like translucent floors in a crystal building: at bottom a green circuit board with tiny transistors, above it a terminal screen with green text, above that colorful code scrolling, above that a web of neural network nodes pulsing with golden light. Each layer glows a different color. Warm orange highlights. Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes

panels.text: Above those transistors, an operating system is juggling thousands of tasks. Above the OS, a programming language is translating human ideas into machine instructions. Above that language, a neural network is predicting the next word you might want to read. And above that, an AI agent might be writing code, running tests, and fixing its own mistakes.

Every layer depends on the one below it. Every layer hides the complexity beneath it and presents a simpler interface to the layer above. This idea — abstraction — is the single most powerful concept in the history of computing. It is the reason a 14-year-old can build a website without understanding quantum physics.

panels.caption: Eight layers, ninety years of human ingenuity

panels.text: In this final issue, we are going to see the whole stack. All of it. From physics to your prompt. And then we are going to look at what comes next — and what role you might play in it.
Every one of those layers was somebody's life work. Let's meet them all — one more time.
